Further- more, increased mortality was not seen in patients in the original DATATOP trial1 after an average follow-up time of 8.2 years. However, it was noted that the delay of disability observed in the early phase of selegiline therapy1,7 was not associated with long- er life during follow-up.26 A recent systematic review23 has also found no convincing evidence that selective monoamine oxidase type B inhibitors (selegiline and lazabemide) significantly delay disease progression in early Parkinson’s disease and routine use is not recommended. 1.
